w:r.w:t: Frye Platform — Draft Client Requirements Answers
Updated October 23, 2026 with five explicit owner decisions. Existing unverified technical details remain marked for confirmation.

Status key: OWNER CONFIRMED = explicit owner decision; ESTABLISHED = previously agreed requirement; PARTLY CONFIRMED = some details still open; RECOMMENDED; CONFIRM = proposed control awaiting approval; TO BE CONFIRMED = no settled answer.
Project understanding
1. What is the main purpose of the Frye platform for your team?
ESTABLISHED

Create Redline Trading powered by AI: a trader-facing dashboard that presents the existing Frye backend’s market intelligence, Elliott Wave structure, strategy status, broker/account visibility and trade journal. The current effort is a frontend replacement/integration, not a rewrite of the engines.
2. Who will use the platform, and what should each type of user be able to do?
OWNER CONFIRMED

The owner/trader and authorized programmers are initial users. The platform is intended to support paying subscribers in the future. Subscribers should have secure individual logins and access to authorized dashboard data and relevant alerts. Exact subscription tiers, administrative roles, subscriber trading privileges and launch timing: To be confirmed.
3. Which screens, dashboards or workflows are most important to you?
ESTABLISHED

Market Meter (ES and SPY), Index & Sectors, Elliott Wave Degrees, charts, Strategies and Trade Management, and Journal are top priorities. Add morning and intraday briefings. Preserve the existing Redline branding.
4. What should the platform help you decide, monitor or record?
ESTABLISHED

Monitor market participation, sector breadth, liquidity/tactical states and seven Elliott Wave degrees; evaluate ES trade location, direction, permission, risk/targets; inspect broker positions; and record per-contract trade outcomes.
Market data and instruments
5. Which stocks, indexes, futures, options or other instruments must be supported?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

ES futures are the main trading and execution instrument, including micro ES when relevant. SPY is a market meter/context input, not the Strategy 1 execution instrument. Broad indexes and sector constituents support market internals. Exact required stock, options and other futures symbols: To be confirmed.
6. Which timeframes and market sessions do you need?
ESTABLISHED

Intraday 1m (diagnostic), 5m (participation), 10m (Strategy 1 context), 30m, 1H, 4H and EOD. Use ES Globex session for futures and the regular U.S. equity session when validating equity internals. Display times in America/Phoenix.
7. Which data providers or subscriptions do you already have?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Existing Schwab/thinkorswim connectivity and account reads; FRED API key configured, though a maintenance response was observed. Additional quote/breadth providers and paid subscriptions: To be confirmed from deployed environment and billing.
8. What data freshness and history do you expect?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Show data as soon as each backend refresh is published; retain existing 10m and 30m market-internals archives, 1H/4H/EOD reads and replay data where available. Exact latency SLA, archive lifespan and full historical coverage: To be confirmed.
9. Are there provider limits, licensing rules or symbols we must follow?
TO BE CONFIRMED

Developer must inventory every data provider, allowed symbols, API rate limits, display/redistribution terms and whether third-party market data can be shown to future customers. Do not assume the current subscriptions permit commercial redistribution.
Codebase and backend behavior
10. Which parts of the existing codebase should be kept, changed or removed?
ESTABLISHED

Keep the existing backend engines, canonical trade logic, snapshots, archives, and journal. Build a separate frontend. Add read-only API adapters only where necessary; remove old frontend code only after parity testing. Do not change production trading logic without separate approval.
11. Which engines or calculations are required for the first version?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

First version should consume existing Market Meter, Engine 25 index/sector internals, Engine 22 Elliott Waves, Engines 26/27 strategies, Engines 3/4/6/7/9 decision/sizing/plan outputs, Engine 29 tactical layer, Engine 8 broker/paper status and Engine 10 journal. Exact production endpoint readiness: verify.
12. What should each engine receive as input and return as output?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Use each engine’s existing canonical inputs/outputs rather than redefine them. Example: Engine 22 returns wave hierarchy/lifecycle and Fib watches; Engine 25 returns breadth/participation plus session/freshness; Engine 26 returns zone/trip status; Engine 6 returns permission; Engine 7 sizing; Engine 9 official plan; Engine 10 per-contract journal. Require a field-level API manifest before coding.
13. What business rules should determine a signal, score, level, alert or trade decision?
ESTABLISHED

Backend alone decides signals and trading authority. For Strategy 1, Engine 3 reaction, Engine 4 primary 5m participation, Engine 6 paper permission, Engine 7 sizing and Engine 9 plan must be used as designed. Engine 26 resets a completed trip to NEUTRAL on target-zone midpoint touch. Frontend must not reconstruct signals from colors.
14. Which calculations or outputs are still unclear and need your definition?
TO BE CONFIRMED

Need an audit of actual canonical endpoint payloads, field status, new seven-degree Engine 22 / 27 alignment, final live-vs-paper order policy and any unresolved engine calculations. Record discrepancies; do not guess expected outputs.
Frontend and API behavior
15. What should each important page or chart show?
ESTABLISHED

Market Meter: ES/SPY state; Index & Sectors: breadth, advance/decline, volume, coverage, timeframes and freshness; Elliott Waves: seven degrees, Fib targets and touched levels; Charts: ES price/levels; Strategies: gate status, plan and risk; Journal: broker accounts and individual contract outcomes.
16. Which values, states or messages must be visible to the user?
ESTABLISHED

Always surface symbol, last backend timestamp, session/freshness, engine state, direction, blockers, permission, zone/targets/stops and data availability. Show touched Fib levels green only when backend confirms the touch. Journal shows open/closed contract states and realized-only metrics.
17. How quickly should the screen update after new market data arrives?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Update promptly after new backend snapshots arrive; never claim faster real-time data than available. Engine 29 has a 5-minute update schedule; other snapshots follow their own 10m/30m/1H/4H/EOD jobs. Browser polling / push approach and latency target: To be confirmed.
18. What should the user see when data is delayed, missing or invalid?
ESTABLISHED

Clearly label STALE, LAST VALID, UNAVAILABLE or ERROR and show the last valid timestamp; do not silently display old values as live. Hide/disable actionable trade controls when required permission or data is missing. Preserve explanatory reason codes.
19. Are there existing API responses or screen examples we should match?
ESTABLISHED

Use the existing deployed dashboard, backend strategy snapshot (including services/core/data/strategy-snapshot-es.json), Engine 25 archives, Engine 22 seven-degree outputs and Engine 10 contract-level journal as references. Capture matching API samples and old/new screenshots during acceptance testing.
Trading and broker use
20. Do you need read-only account information, paper trading, live trading, or a combination?
OWNER CONFIRMED — TARGET SCOPE

The platform must ultimately support both PAPER and LIVE trading, alongside read-only broker/account information. Existing paper-testing and broker-observation functions do not establish that live order placement is currently operational. Live execution requires separately designed, tested and owner-approved controls before enablement. Whether live trading is included in the first frontend launch: To be confirmed.
21. Which accounts, instruments and order types are allowed?
OWNER CONFIRMED — ACCOUNT MODEL

There are seven Schwab/thinkorswim accounts, intended to operate as one account per trading strategy. The programmer must preserve distinct account identities, orders, positions and journal reporting for each strategy/account. ES and micro ES are known instruments. Exact seven account-to-strategy mappings, permitted futures/options, order types, and account permissions: To be confirmed by the owner; do not infer them from previous intraday/swing account examples.
22. What approvals or safety rules are required before an order can be sent?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

The owner personally approves all trading-engine code changes. For PAPER execution, retain backend permission, direction, sizing, locking and official management-plan gates. For LIVE execution, implement separate owner-approved authorization, per-account restrictions, risk limits, safe order lifecycle, reconciliation and an emergency disable mechanism. Never equate approval of code changes with approval of individual live orders. Whether manual confirmation is required for each live order: To be confirmed.
23. What must immediately stop trading or disable an account?
TO BE CONFIRMED

Before live trading is enabled, the owner must approve exact hard-stop conditions and thresholds. Proposed safeguards include lost broker authorization, stale/invalid data, failed engine/sizing permission, daily loss limit, rejected/repeated orders, broker reconciliation mismatch, manual account disable and emergency stop. No specific threshold is approved in this document.
24. How should trades, positions and decisions be recorded?
ESTABLISHED

Engine 10 must journal immutable broker transaction lineage, tradeId and per-contract contractId; track entry/exit, partial closes, status, realized points/P&L and account classification separately. Open contracts must not be counted in realized closed-contract metrics.
AI and alerts
25. What may the AI assistant explain or summarize?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Explain engine readings, market breadth, Elliott Wave/fib paths, official strategy blockers, trading plans, journal performance, and morning/intraday market context with timestamps and uncertainty. AI content must be separated from canonical engine decisions.
26. What must the AI assistant never recommend or do?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

The AI may explain authorized backend outputs but must not fabricate market data, override approved engine decisions or expose secrets. It must never place live broker orders or alter strategies without the separately required owner-approved authority and controls. Whether AI may propose trades for user confirmation, and any personalized subscriber advice rules: To be confirmed.
27. Which events should create an alert?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Useful alerts: strategy readiness or block transitions, wave targets touched, material market breadth/tactical changes, stale scanner/engine output, broker reconnect needed and Schwab OAuth approaching expiry. Exact alert list, thresholds and frequency: To be confirmed.
28. Who should receive each alert and through which channel?
OWNER CONFIRMED — TARGET SCOPE

The system should eventually send individualized alerts to each dashboard subscriber according to that subscriber’s subscriptions, strategies and preferences. The owner should receive operational and broker alerts; Pushover was previously discussed for the Schwab Day-6 renewal reminder. Subscriber alert channels, opt-ins, severity levels and launch timing: To be confirmed.
29. What should happen when a data feed, engine or broker connection fails?
RECOMMENDED; CONFIRM

Show outage and last successful timestamps, retry safely, log diagnostics and alert the responsible maintainer. Trading permissions should fail closed where required inputs are missing. Do not duplicate orders or overwrite immutable archives; specify recovery and escalation rules.
Data, security and maintenance
30. What information must be stored, and for how long?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Retain canonical engine snapshots, 10m/30m market internals archives as configured, replay evidence, journal contracts/transactions, engine decisions and operational logs. Monthly cleanup was permitted for some 10m archives. Exact retention by class, broker data retention and backups: To be confirmed.
31. Who should be allowed to view, edit or delete data?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

The owner personally approves all changes to trading engines. The platform is intended for paying subscribers with individually scoped access; subscribers must not gain permission to change shared engine logic or view another user’s sensitive account data. Exact role permissions for viewing, editing, deleting, account linkage and subscriber data: To be confirmed.
32. How should credentials and API keys be shared securely?
ESTABLISHED

Use managed secrets (for example Render environment variables and GitHub Actions secrets), never browser bundles, chat messages, repository files or this questionnaire. Give the programmer access through role-based platform invitations and rotate/revoke access as needed.
33. What audit history or activity record is required?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Preserve deployment/change logs, snapshot/source timestamps, engine state transitions, trade permission decisions, broker transaction identities, account actions, and journal corrections. Exact retention, tamper-proofing and user-action auditing: To be confirmed.
34. Who will own ongoing maintenance and approve future code changes?
OWNER CONFIRMED

The owner personally approves every change to trading engines. Programmers may audit, propose and implement changes in separate branches but must not merge or deploy engine changes without explicit owner approval. The new programmer may maintain the new frontend under agreed access controls. Detailed frontend change approvals, incident response, on-call support and deployment ownership: To be confirmed.
Expected result
35. What does a correct result look like for each major feature?
ESTABLISHED

Each section reproduces the backend’s canonical values from the same timestamp; seven wave degrees and touched flags are accurate; market freshness is explicit; strategy signals and blocks are unchanged; journal contract/P&L reconciliation is correct; new frontend works independently before cutover.
36. What examples, sample data or expected outputs can you provide?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Provide production-read-only API payloads, ES snapshot examples, Engine 25 archive files, Engine 22 Fib/lifecycle screenshots and Engine 10 known PAPER/REAL journal cases. Verify exact file and endpoint locations and sanitize broker/secret information before sharing.
37. What known problems or incorrect results should we fix first?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Known issues to check: 30m scanner runs crossing a timestamp boundary and attempting different immutable payloads for the same archive key; occasional stale Engine 22/27 alignment; Fibonacci touched-level display; market data freshness; Schwab OAuth reconnection; and strategy verification timing. Recheck current status before labeling any issue still open.
38. Which requirements are essential, and which can be added later?
PARTLY CONFIRMED

Essential foundation: preserve backend engines, separate frontend, canonical API contracts, ES/SPY meters, Index/Sectors, seven-degree Waves, Strategies, Journal, freshness/error handling, account separation and parity testing. Confirmed longer-term goals: PAPER and LIVE trading, one Schwab account per strategy across seven accounts, paying subscribers and personalized subscriber alerts. Exact phased launch order, live-trading release gates and subscriber commercialization requirements: To be confirmed.
39. What questions about the current codebase would you like us to explain?
ESTABLISHED

Please document: canonical endpoint/owner for every panel; which jobs generate/persist each output; field schemas; freshness and time zone rules; paper vs REAL trading authorization boundary; archive key/idempotency behavior; Engine 22→27 synchronization; journal reconciliation; security, rate limits and deploy/rollback procedure.
Remaining decisions and technical verification
Confirm whether the FIRST new-frontend release includes live broker order entry, or launches paper/read-only before a later live release.
Supply the seven strategy names and the corresponding Schwab account mapping securely (account labels or masked last four digits only); specify allowed order types.
Define subscriber roles, pricing/tier access and launch timing, including whether subscribers may connect their own brokerage accounts.
Verify licensed market data/subscriptions, distribution rights to paying subscribers, retention periods and API rate limits.
Approve live risk limits, emergency stops, per-order confirmation policy, and individualized alert channels/preferences.
Security note: Do not attach passwords, token values, API keys or full brokerage account numbers.
